checks.lead: Constantine I (27 February 272 – 22 May 337), also known as Constantine the Great, was a Roman emperor from AD 306 to 337, co-ruling as part of the Tetrarchy until 324. The first Roman emperor to convert to Christianity, Constantine played a pivotal role in elevating the religion's status in the Roman Empire, with the Edict of Milan decriminalising its practice and ceasing Christian persecution. He founded the city of Constantinople (now Istanbul) and made it the capital of the Empire, which it remained for over a millennium.
